title: KPGS Frontier Harness — Provider-Independent Capability POC
outcome: Prove one governed vertical slice in which a disposable intake surface requests a rented capability while KPGS retains routing, evaluation, receipts, durable-state authority, modality authority and rollback control.

included: Normalize a synthetic Fillout/Zite-style event into kpgs.capability_request.v1
Route a permitted synthetic request through a deterministic Google AI mock renter
Emit kpgs.capability_receipt.v1 with non-canonical provider output
Prepare a Snowflake analytical-copy row without semantic input
Compute a local SHA-256 commitment and Solana devnet anchor intent
Emit kpgs.modality_contract.v1 with renderer authority explicitly false
excluded: Production provider credentials or durable secrets
Live Google AI, ElevenLabs, Snowflake or Solana calls
Publishing private or restricted input to external providers
Replacing local sovereign storage with Snowflake
Giving renderers or rented models semantic authority

interfaces.name: Structured intake
interfaces.contract: Fillout/Zite-style events are untrusted input and are normalized before routing.

interfaces.name: Rented capability
interfaces.contract: Provider adapter output is non-canonical until KPGS evaluates it; v0.1 uses a deterministic Google AI mock.

interfaces.name: Analytics copy
interfaces.contract: Snowflake receives governed metadata/digests only; local sovereign state remains canonical.

interfaces.name: Public proof
interfaces.contract: Solana devnet receives only a SHA-256 commitment payload and no private data.

interfaces.name: Modality
interfaces.contract: Renderer choice is governed separately from semantic authority and always retains a text fallback in v0.1.

constraints: Provider capability must remain replaceable and cannot become KPGS dependency.
External processing must be policy-gated by data classification.
No durable secret may be committed to the repository.
Public anchors may contain commitment material only.
Snowflake is an analytical copy and not local sovereign state.
ElevenLabs is a renderer capability and cannot own semantic authority.
Input is never treated as authority merely because a human-facing form supplied it.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Synthetic Fillout-style input normalizes into a strict capability request with untrusted source status and explicit policy.
The capability router selects a replaceable provider adapter and v0.1 cannot claim live model execution.
Provider output is digest-bound, non-canonical, and KPGS remains semantic evaluator/authority.
Snowflake telemetry contains metadata/digests but no semantic input or private payload.
Solana anchor intent is devnet-only, commitment-only, and structurally excludes private data.
Modality contracts separate rendering from semantic authority and retain a native text fallback.
A dependency-free validator executes the full synthetic vertical slice and verifies governing invariants.

verification_plan.evidence: router decision must report adapter_mode=mock until a live capability lease is supplied.
snowflake/bootstrap.sql defines only metadata/digest columns and validation forbids SEMANTIC_INPUT.
modality-contract.schema.json fixes renderer_has_semantic_authority=false; dry-run preserves native-text fallback.
Dependency-free validator imports frontier_harness.py, runs synthetic fixture, and verifies receipt/telemetry/anchor/modality invariants.

rollback_plan.trigger: Any provider becomes a hidden authority/dependency, private data can reach the public anchor, or the POC conflicts with existing KPGS vNext invariants.
rollback_plan.procedure: Revert the Frontier Harness commit/PR. No production provider credential, mainnet state, or estate release depends on v0.1.
